description:
F124 (Sprint 51): Manage Rules category / sub-type DISPLAY. Verifies that rule rows expose their category and sub-type as accessible names, that the rule-details dialog presents Category and Sub-Type as labelled fields, and that the sub-type filter chips narrow the list. READ-ONLY: navigates and toggles filter chips only -- creates, edits and deletes nothing -- and clears every filter before exiting, so the DB-drift guard stays green. SELECTORS AND INTERACTION MODEL VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-28 against dev build 0.5.8.

FOUR HARNESS FACTS drove this script's shape. All were established by failing runs, not assumed:

(1) USE ww_invoke, NOT ww_click, FOR FLUTTER CONTROLS. ww_click (which tries UIA InvokePattern then falls back to a physical mouse click) repeatedly reported success WITHOUT activating the control from a cold-launched app -- the Settings button reported success while the app stayed on the home screen. ww_invoke fires InvokePattern directly and works. ww_click is used ONLY where a physical mouse press is genuinely wanted (TabBar tabs, which project as Text nodes).

(2) A STEP REPORTING SUCCESS IS NOT PROOF OF EFFECT. It proves the action was DISPATCHED. Because `ww_assert*` is NOT replayable by the script runner, the only in-script evidence that something happened is a FOLLOWING step that can only resolve if the app actually advanced. Every navigation below is followed by such a step; that pairing is the real assertion.

(3) FLUTTER BUILDS ITS UIA SEMANTICS TREE LAZILY, IN RESPONSE TO A QUERY -- NOT ON A TIMER. On a freshly launched app the first tree query returns an opaque single 'FLUTTERVIEW' pane; the second returns the full tree. A 10-second wait does NOT help, because waiting is not the trigger. The leading ww_window_state acts as that priming query.

(4) THE SEARCH BOX CANNOT BE CLEARED BY AUTOMATION on this build: ww_type clearFirst:true APPENDS (observed 'museum'+'gmail' -> 'museumgmail'), ww_clear throws a COM HRESULT, and ctrl+a/Delete does not reach the Flutter field. This script therefore NEVER types into the search box -- it uses the stateless filter chips, which are idempotent and expose a 'Clear' button that exists ONLY while a filter is active.

testCases.title: Rule rows expose category + sub-type; details dialog labels them; chips narrow and restore

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY (fact 3): forces Flutter to build its semantics subtree. Without this the first control lookup on a cold app resolves 0 elements.
Settings is account-scoped: this opens an in-Flutter 'Select Account' overlay, not the Settings screen directly.

The picker entry resolves BY NAME thanks to the Sprint 51 F129 accessibility work, and dismisses because that Semantics node carries its own onTap. Before the 2026-07-28 fix this entry projected as two stacked same-named Buttons and the outer one had no handler -- the click reported success and the dialog stayed open.

PROOF OF ARRIVAL: the General tab exists only once Settings is actually open, so resolving it proves the picker really dismissed. Tabs project as Text nodes; useInvokePattern:false forces the physical mouse press they need.
F124 entry point. Manage Rules projects as a correctly-named Button.
PROOF OF ARRIVAL: 'Test a pattern against sample emails' exists only on the Manage Rules screen.
steps.selector: type=Button[name='Test a pattern against sample emails']

steps._comment: PROOF OF ARRIVAL on the F25 tool, then straight back -- this also confirms the Manage Rules top bar is live.
F124 CORE -- CATEGORY chips carry their live counts in the accessible name. Prefix-matched because counts are data-dependent.
PROOF OF EFFECT: 'Clear' is rendered ONLY while a filter is active, so its presence proves the chip actually filtered the list. It is also the state-restore.
F124 CORE -- the four SUB-TYPE chips, the Sprint 50 classifications under test.

F124 CORE -- with the TLD filter active, each visible row exposes an accessible name stating BOTH its category and its sub-type. Resolving this exact string IS the F124 row-display contract, and proves the filter selected matching rows.
steps.selector: type=Button[name='Header / From category, Top-Level Domain sub-type. View rule details']

steps._comment: F124 STRONGEST EVIDENCE: the details dialog renders Category and Sub-Type as explicitly LABELLED fields. Resolving both labels proves the dialog opened AND that the classification is presented as named fields rather than free text. NOTE: static Text nodes do NOT support InvokePattern ('Element does not support InvokePattern. ControlType: Text' -- observed 2026-07-28), so these two steps must use ww_click with useInvokePattern:false. The click is harmless on a label; the point is that the selector RESOLVES.
The classification VALUES, not just the field labels -- this rule is a Top-Level Domain rule in the Header / From category, so both values must be present in the dialog.

Close the dialog WITHOUT editing -- read-only. WARNING: name='Close' also matches the window titlebar Close (#Close); a stray match would exit the app. Safe here ONLY because the dialog is known open and its Close resolves first (verified live -- app still alive afterwards). Do not reuse this selector when no dialog is open.
STATE RESTORE: drop the TLD filter so the screen returns to the unfiltered view it was found in (Sprint 37 policy).
PROOF OF RESTORE: Refresh resolves on the live, unfiltered Manage Rules screen.

PROOF OF RETURN HOME: the account ROW is present only on the home screen. Invoking it would start a scan, so this step deliberately targets the home-screen 'View Scan History' button instead -- present on home, absent on Manage Rules -- and the following Back returns from it. Read-only either way.
